title: Given a scenario, use Microsoft Windows operating system features and tools

subtopics.heading: Task Manager
subtopics.notes:
Real-time view of Windows system activity. Launch:
- Ctrl+Alt+Delete > Task Manager
- Right-click the taskbar > Task Manager
- Ctrl+Shift+Esc (fastest)

Key tabs:
- Processes: every running app and background process with CPU, memory, disk, network, GPU columns. Sort and add columns by right-clicking
- Performance: live 60-second graphs for CPU, memory, disk, network, GPU
- Services: list of Windows services. Start / stop / restart. Same data as the Services applet (services.msc)
- Startup: applications that launch at boot. Enable / disable individually for troubleshooting
- Users: connected users (local AND remote). Disconnect any user from here
subtopics.whyOnExam: Know which tab answers which troubleshooting question: CPU spike = Performance, slow boot = Startup, what's connected = Users.
subtopics.commonTrap: Confusing the Services tab (Task Manager) with the Services applet. Both manage services but the applet has more options.

subtopics.heading: Microsoft Management Console + snap-ins
subtopics.notes:
mmc.exe opens an empty console. Add snap-ins via File > Add/Remove Snap-in. Save the layout as a .msc file to re-open later.

Common snap-ins (each also runs standalone):
- eventvwr.msc - Event Viewer. Windows logs separated into Application, Security, Setup, System. Levels: Information, Warning, Error, Critical, Successful audit, Failure audit. Filter logs to find specific events fast
- diskmgmt.msc - Disk Management. View drives, partitions, file systems. Change drive letters, shrink / extend volumes, mirror. Destructive - back up first
- taskschd.msc - Task Scheduler. Run programs on a schedule or trigger. Edit Triggers / Actions / Conditions / Settings tabs
- devmgmt.msc - Device Manager. Hardware grouped by category (printers, display adapters, etc.). Update / disable / uninstall drivers
- certmgr.msc - Certificate Manager. View / add / remove certificates including trusted Certification Authorities
- lusrmgr.msc - Local Users and Groups. Built-in: Administrator, Guest. Predefined groups: Administrators, Users, Backup Operators, Power Users
- perfmon.msc - Performance Monitor. Long-term metric collection with alerts. Hundreds of counters available
- gpedit.msc - Local Group Policy Editor (single machine). For Active Directory environments use gpmc.msc (Group Policy Management Console)
subtopics.whyOnExam: Memorize the .msc filenames - the exam tests them directly. eventvwr, diskmgmt, taskschd, devmgmt, certmgr, lusrmgr, perfmon, gpedit, gpmc.
subtopics.commonTrap: Picking gpedit.msc when the scenario describes a domain-wide policy push. gpedit is local; gpmc is the Active Directory tool.

subtopics.heading: Additional Windows tools
subtopics.notes:
System Information (msinfo32.exe)
- Read-only overview. System Summary shows OS, processor, BIOS, boot device, RAM
- Categories: Hardware Resources, Components, Software Environment
- Useful for unfamiliar machines - one screen, everything

Resource Monitor (resmon.exe)
- Real-time view combined with detailed statistics
- Tabs for CPU, Memory, Disk, Network
- More granular than Task Manager's Performance tab

System Configuration (msconfig.exe)
- Tabs: General, Boot, Services, Startup, Tools
- Boot: select OS, safe boot options, boot log, GUI on/off
- Startup: now redirects to Task Manager
- Tools: launch other utilities (Event Viewer, Resource Monitor, etc.)

Disk Cleanup (cleanmgr.exe)
- Categorize and delete unneeded files: temp internet, downloaded program files, recycle bin, Windows error reports

Disk Defragment (dfrgui.exe, defrag command)
- ONLY for spinning hard drives. Do NOT defrag SSDs (no performance benefit, wears the drive)
- Default schedule runs weekly
- Shows efficiency percent; nothing to do at 98%+

Registry Editor (regedit.exe)
- Hierarchical config database. Top-level hives all start with HKEY:
  - HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT
  - HKEY_CURRENT_USER
  - HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
  - HKEY_USERS
  - HKEY_CURRENT_CONFIG
- Always export the hive before editing - File > Export
- UAC prompts at launch because changes can wreck the OS
subtopics.whyOnExam: regedit hive names and msinfo32 vs resmon vs msconfig are common targets. Know what each one is FOR.
subtopics.commonTrap: Defragging an SSD. The exam will test this directly. SSDs do not need defragmentation and may be harmed by it.
